events.body:
RIDER: We looked into your cancellation and the $6.61 fee stands. You cancelled yourself, and the app shows the driver was already near your pickup and waiting for several minutes before you did. Cancelling more than three minutes after a driver accepts is chargeable, so no refund is due here. If you'd like us to reconsider, you can make a discretionary appeal for RydeHELP credit within 30 days; any relief is granted as a Ryde voucher, not cash. Nothing changes on your account from this decision.

DRIVER: We reviewed the cancellation on this trip. You waited near the pickup point for several minutes before the rider cancelled, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is confirmed and stands in your favour. It's paid to you as Ryde voucher credit under our usual process — no action is needed from you. The rider cancelled voluntarily, so this outcome doesn't affect your account or your standing.

ruling.recommended_action: Confirm the $6.61 cancellation fee stands; advise rider that any relief is a discretionary RydeHELP appeal under NS-7 (voucher form, within 30 days).
ruling.reasoning:
Cancellation was made by the rider, so NS-0 routes the case to NS-4 rather than NS-1/NS-2 [F4][NS-0]. The booking was an on-demand instant match accepted at 08:40:00 and cancelled at 08:46:40, i.e. 6 min 40 s (400 s) after matching, far outside the 3-minute free-cancellation window [F4][NS-4]. The $6.61 fee is therefore chargeable as a matter of rule; the rider's own message "Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel" confirms the cancellation was voluntary and unrelated to driver conduct [F11][NS-4].

The complaint's premise ("the driver had not even arrived") is contradicted by the system records: the driver was first within 200 m of the pickup at 08:41:35, stayed within 200 m for 5 min 5 s before cancellation, with a closest approach of 39 m, and stood stationary 41 m from the pickup from 08:42:00 to 08:46:40 [F1][F2][F3][F5][NS-4]. Even taking the rider's side of the tap conflict (F6 asserts a tap at 08:42:15 while F7 records driver_pressed_here_at as null), the tap requirement is an NS-1 element for driver-initiated no-show cancellations only, and NS-0/NS-4 decide a rider cancellation on the 3-minute clock alone [F6][F7][NS-0][NS-4].

No ancillary charge arises: the fee on record is the published flat $6.61 at a 1.0× surge with no other added items [F8][F9][FARE-1]. There were no traffic incidents or congestion bands and weather was fair, so no RD-4 reasonable-cause or external-cause argument bears on the fare [F13][F14][F15][NS-4]. Because no fee is refundable, the amount is nil. The rider's remedy, if any, is the discretionary voucher-based appeal under NS-7, not a rule-based refund [F4][NS-7].

Both advocates ultimately request no_action and neither side's facts establish a charge that fails its own conditions; the rider's profile (2 disputes in 90 d, 1 upheld) and the driver's profile (699 trips, 0 upheld) are noted but cannot decide the case, and no RD-6/NS-2 account action is triggered [F16][F17][RD-6][NS-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's only remaining avenue is discretionary appeal, not a rule-based refund: NS-4 fixes the fee on the 3-minute matching clock once the rider cancels past 3 minutes [F4][NS-4], and NS-7 expressly makes any voucher refund a matter of Ryde's discretion, so the complaint yields no refundable amount [NS-7]. The rider advocate itself conceded this in rebuttal to D1/D5 [F11][NS-4].

certificate: ✓ NS-4 rider cancelled more than 3 min after matching [case] 400 s after acceptance (F4)

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: This is a rider-cancelled instant booking, so the $6.61 fee is governed solely by NS-4: cancellations within 3 minutes of matching are not chargeable, and this ride was matched at 08:40:00 with the rider cancelling at 08:46:40, i.e. 6 min 40 s later — beyond the free window.

The driver's own GPS record contradicts the premise of the rider's complaint: the driver was first within 200 m of the pickup at 08:41:35 and remained within 200 m for 5 min 5 s before the cancellation, so he had in fact arrived, and the fare file confirms the $6.61 fee that NS-4 makes chargeable in that situation.

The driver also satisfied every condition of a passenger no-show cancellation — he tapped "I'm Here" at 08:42:15 while 39 m from the pickup (closest approach 39 m at 08:42:40) and stayed within 200 m for 4 min 25 s after the tap, including standing stationary 41 m away from 08:42:00 to 08:46:40 — so no NS-1/NS-2 defect exists that would convert the fee into a refund.

The rider's own message "Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel" confirms the cancellation was the rider's free choice and not caused by any driver conduct, so nothing in FARE-1 (an unpublished or non-qualifying charge) is triggered by this fee.

There is no factual basis to attack the charge on any other ground: no traffic incidents or congestion bands were recorded on the route during the trip window and weather was fair, and the driver has no upheld no-show or route dispute against him, so no fee_waived or partial refund applies.

The rider's principal grievance — that the driver "had not even arrived" — is unsupported by the system records, and NS-4 expressly states that a driver not yet being at the pickup is not a ground for fee-free cancellation; the rider's remedy, if any, is a discretionary human appeal under NS-7 rather than a rule-based refund.

weaknesses: The rider genuinely did not board and cancelled unilaterally; F11 ("plans changed, I will cancel") is the rider's own admission and the other side will use it to show the loss of the driver's time, and F17 shows that driver has 699 trips in 90 d with 0 upheld disputes, making a rule-based fee waiver very hard to argue.

The 3-minute free-cancellation window in NS-4 had long expired on the face of F4 (cancel at 6 min 40 s), so the only remaining arguments are non-rule-based: the driver tapped "I'm Here" only 2 min 15 s after matching and stayed parked rather than departing, but NS-4 gives a rider no waiver for a driver who was in fact present (F2, F6), and NS-7 makes the $6.61 refund a voucher at Ryde's discretion, not a cash entitlement.
The complaint's factual premise ("the driver had not even arrived") is directly contradicted by F2/F5/F6, so any claim built on it is void and cannot carry the case.

claims.assertion: This is an on-demand booking cancelled by the rider 6 min 40 s after acceptance (08:40:00 → 08:46:40), i.e. well past the 3-minute post-matching window, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is valid under NS-4 and no refund is due.

The driver did arrive and wait: GPS puts him within 200 m of the pickup from 08:41:35, stationary 41 m from the pickup for 4 min 40 s (08:42:00–08:46:40), so the rider's claim that 'the driver had not even arrived' is contradicted by the system record.

The platform's own timeline records the driver's arrival at 08:41:35, and the rider cancelled only 5 min 5 s after that recorded arrival, confirming the rider had ample time to board before cancelling.
The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 08:42:15 while 39 m from the pickup and remained within 200 m for 4 min 25 s afterwards, satisfying the arrival/waiting preconditions of NS-1 for the fee to stand.
The rider's own chat message at 08:45 states 'Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel', which shows the cancellation was the rider's own change of plan, not any driver failure or delay.
No traffic congestion or incident was recorded on the route in the trip window and weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain, so nothing external prevented the driver from being at the pickup as promised.
The fare record shows a flat $6.61 cancellation fee with a 1.0× surge multiplier and no other added charges, so there is no overcharge element in this dispute.

weaknesses: F7 (timeline) states the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' (driver_pressed_here_at is null), which directly conflicts with F6 (arrival tap at 08:42:15); the rider will argue the NS-1 tap requirement is not met and rely on F7 over my client's chat statement F12.

F2/F3 put the driver's closest approach at 39–41 m and his stationary position 41 m from the pickup; although within the 200 m data-layer radius, the rider may argue he was not exactly at the designated pick-up point, and Ryde has not published the exact radius (vacancy G2).

The rider's profile shows 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days (F16), which the rider could use to argue their complaint pattern is credible, even though my client's profile (F17) shows 699 trips in 90 days with 0 upheld disputes.

points.response: Conceded as accurate on the timing — the rider cancelled 6 min 40 s after matching (F4), past the NS-4 free window, so the fee is chargeable as a matter of rule and my client's only remaining avenue is the discretionary human appeal in NS-7, not a rule-based refund.

Conceded: the GPS record does show the driver present, first within 200 m at 08:41:35 and stationary 41 m away from 08:42:00 to 08:46:40 (F2, F3), so the 'he had not even arrived' premise of the complaint cannot be sustained and I withdraw any claim built on it.

Accepted — F5 records platform arrival at 08:41:35 and the rider cancelled 5 min 5 s later (F4); I only note that presence at the pickup is not itself a fee condition under NS-4, which turns on the 3-minute matching clock.

The driver's NS-1 tap reliance is void on the record: F6 asserts a tap at 08:42:15 while F7 states driver_pressed_here_at is null, and the same source (timeline) cannot establish both, so the tap precondition of NS-1 is unproven against the driver — but under NS-0 and NS-4 that gap does not help my client, because a rider-cancelled on-demand booking is decided on the 3-minute window alone, not on NS-1.

This is the rider's own substantive weakness and the decisive practical fact: F11 shows the cancellation came from a change of plans, and F4 confirms the rider, not the driver, cancelled, which is precisely why the $6.61 stands under NS-4.

Not contested, and it cuts against the driver's own NS-1 framing: F13 and F14 record no incidents or congestion bands and F15 fair weather, so there was no external cause at all — the only cause of the non-trip was the rider's decision in F11.

Accepted: F8 shows a single $6.61 cancellation fee at a 1.0× surge (F9), so there is no FARE-1 unpublished or double-charged item to refund and my client's request remains no_action with the fee standing.
Conceded — the rider's own summary of NS-4 is correct and helps my client: F4 shows cancellation 6 min 40 s after acceptance, far outside the 3-minute free window, so the $6.61 fee is valid.
Agreed and adopted: F2 and F5 (arrival at 08:41:35, 5 min 5 s inside 200 m before cancellation) plus F8/F9 confirm the driver had arrived and the flat $6.61 fee is correctly charged.

Agreed the no-show preconditions are met: F6 records the 08:42:15 "I'm Here" tap at 39 m, F1/F2 show the 39 m closest approach and 5 min 5 s within 200 m, and F3 shows him stationary 41 m away from 08:42:00 to 08:46:40, so NS-1 is satisfied and nothing in NS-2 converts the fee to a refund.

Agreed: F11 ("Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel") shows the cancellation was the rider's own choice, and since the fee is the published $6.61 (F8) there is no unpublished or non-qualifying charge to refund under FARE-1.

Agreed — F13, F14 and F15 record no congestion bands, no incidents and fair weather, and F17 shows the driver has 699 trips in 90 days with 0 upheld disputes, so neither fee_waived nor a partial refund has any basis.

Agreed: the rider's premise that the driver "had not even arrived" is contradicted by F2/F5/F6, and NS-4 gives the rider no waiver for a driver who was in fact present; any relief is discretionary under NS-7, not a rule-based refund.
